historical_references.reference: Saint Yurelia of Bourges was a Benedictine nun and hermitess, born in Brittany around 525 AD. She was the daughter of King Gradlon of Broceliande and is also known as Sainte Foy. After her mother's death, Yurelia was raised by her uncle, Saint Budoc. She became a nun and eventually founded a monastery at Jumieges. Later, she left Jumieges and settled as a hermit in the forest of Bourges, where she lived until her death around 560 AD.

Saint Yurelia of Chur was a Carthusian nun, daughter of Count Gundold of Chur, who lived in the 13th century. She is also known as Ysoldis or Iseult. Born into a noble family, she was educated at the monastery of Chur and later became a nun at the Chur Carthusian convent. She was renowned for her sanctity, and her miracles were widely reported.
